google_adk.name: Google ADK

capture_boundary.capture_api: google.adk.tools.mcp_tool.McpToolset.get_tools, then McpTool.process_llm_request inside an LlmAgent run
capture_boundary.capture_object: google.genai.types.FunctionDeclaration in the LlmRequest.config.tools handed to BaseLlm.generate_content_async
capture_boundary.protocol_version_evidence: Against the 2026-07-28 fixture, ClientSession.initialize inside McpToolset returned protocolVersion 2025-11-25: by default McpToolset opens every session with the legacy initialize handshake and never calls discover. With the documented opt-in ADK_ENABLE_MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL=1, 2.11.0 calls the SDK's negotiate_auto instead: the client sent server/discover, negotiated 2026-07-28, and reached tools/list on stdio and HTTP (data/specs/2026-07-28/measurements/opt-in/google_adk-modern-protocol/protocol/google_adk/stdio-00.jsonl, http.jsonl). The renderer reads the adopted version from ClientSession.adopt, which both the default initialize handshake and negotiate_auto end in, so the opt-in scan completes (data/specs/2026-07-28/measurements/opt-in/google_adk-modern-protocol/scan.json: status measured, negotiated 2026-07-28 through server/discover). No cell comes from the opt-in run; the default handshake still decides the row.

result_boundaries.limitation: The model is a scripted BaseLlm; no google-genai client serialized the request.

google_adk.measurement_note: Google ADK 2.11.0 on mcp 2.0.0 negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server by default, because McpToolset's session manager opens every session with the legacy initialize handshake. With ADK_ENABLE_MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL=1 it probes server/discover and negotiates 2026-07-28; that opt-in scan completes and is published as evidence, and it sets no cell.

stable.label: Defined in the released MCP specification

draft.label: Defined only in a draft revision of the MCP specification

proposed.label: Proposed, not yet in any published specification

deprecated.label: Defined in the released MCP specification but deprecated in this revision, and eligible for removal no earlier than the first revision released on or after 2027-07-28

extension.label: Defined in an official opt-in extension rather than the core specification, and disabled unless both sides negotiate it

support_codes.y: exposed to the agent at the declared capture boundary
support_codes.a: changed at the boundary or reachable only elsewhere
support_codes.x: the adapter cannot negotiate this protocol revision, so no capability is reachable

defaults.inclusion_rule: A framework is listed if it ships a first-party or officially documented MCP adapter. Nothing is excluded on quality grounds.
defaults.order_rule: Alphabetical within language group. No ranking is implied or computed.
defaults.version_policy: Era 0 is the framework release tested for this protocol snapshot. An unmeasured cell means no same-protocol adapter capture was produced.
defaults.green_rule: Every cell answers one question: does this framework expose this MCP capability to the agent at its declared capture boundary? For a value carried in a tool definition, 'y' means the value is present there unchanged. For a protocol feature, 'y' means the adapter gives the agent a working path to it and a scan exercised that path. A capability the framework could support but does not is not 'y'.
defaults.partial_rule: 'a' means the capability is reachable but not on the terms the specification sets: the note must say whether the value was transformed at the boundary, only partly preserved, retained somewhere the agent does not read, or supported only for part of the feature.
defaults.surface_rule: surface.json enumerates what MCP 2026-07-28 defines, and it is maintained separately from what we have measured. Any feature in it without a capability file is published with every cell 'u'. Coverage is therefore computed from the two files rather than asserted, and a feature cannot be quietly dropped from the denominator to make coverage look better.
defaults.note_rule: Every 'a' and 'n' cell must carry a #n note reference naming the exact mechanism, so a status can be checked rather than trusted.
defaults.usage_rule: No adoption weighting is published. We have no defensible source yet, and an invented percentage would be the least trustworthy number on the page.

coverage.note: The feature surface of MCP 2026-07-28, enumerated from the released specification. This file is the denominator: it is what the protocol defines, independent of what we have measured. A feature with a hand-authored file in capabilities/ is measured; every other feature is published as a row whose cells are all 'u'. Coverage is therefore a fact the build computes, not a claim the site makes.
omissions: Skills over MCP is not listed. The spec index advertises it, but /extensions/skills/overview 404s and the only published material is a working-group charter, so there is no wire contract to measure against.

Features removed in this revision (initialize, ping, logging/setLevel, resources/subscribe, notifications/roots/list_changed, Mcp-Session-Id, SSE resumability) are absent by design. They belong to the 2025-11-25 snapshot, not this one.

tool-audio-content.notes: 3 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 8 changed or retained elsewhere, 2 dropped, 18 cannot reach MCP 2026-07-28.

notes_by_num.1: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85 requires mcp>=1.30,<2.0, and on mcp 1.30.0 MCPTool.from_client negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server: MCPSessionProvider opens every session with the legacy initialize handshake.
notes_by_num.2: autogen-ext 0.7.5 imports mcp.shared.context.RequestContext, which the MCP Python SDK removed in 2.0.0, so it cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.
notes_by_num.3: CrewAI 1.15.26 requires MCP Python SDK 1.28.x (crewai pins mcp>=1.28.1,<1.29), so it cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26 requires MCP Python SDK 1.28.x (crewai pins mcp>=1.28.1,<1.29), so its native crewai.mcp client cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.
notes_by_num.5: DSPy 3.4.0: with the default `result_mode="text"`, `Tool.acall` returns the audio block as the MCP content object when the result has no text (direct: `y`). In a `dspy.ReAct` run the observation the model reads is that object's Python repr, `«type='audio' data='...' mime_type='audio/wav' ...»` (react: `a`). When a result carries any text block, `_convert_mcp_tool_result` returns the text alone and drops the audio block at both boundaries.
notes_by_num.6: Google ADK 2.11.0 on mcp 2.0.0 negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server by default, because McpToolset's session manager opens every session with the legacy initialize handshake. With ADK_ENABLE_MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL=1 it probes server/discover and negotiates 2026-07-28; that opt-in scan completes and is published as evidence, and it sets no cell.
notes_by_num.7: mcp-haystack 1.5.2 on mcp 2.2.0 negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server, because MCPClient opens every session with the legacy initialize handshake.
notes_by_num.8: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2 requires mcp<2.0.0, so it cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2 requires mcp<2.0.0, so it cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.
notes_by_num.10: llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0 on mcp 2.0.0 negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server, because BasicMCPClient opens every session with the legacy initialize handshake.
notes_by_num.11: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0 declares the MCP Python SDK below 2.0 (mcp>=1.24.0,<2, through its `all` extra); on mcp 1.30.0 it negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server.
notes_by_num.12: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: the audio block is re-serialized as JSON inside a text output item. The base64 payload and `audio/wav` MIME type are all still present, but the agent receives them as characters rather than as audio content.
notes_by_num.13: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0 requires mcp<2.0, and on mcp 1.26.0 its plugin negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server: MCPPluginBase opens every session with the legacy initialize handshake.
notes_by_num.14: smolagents 1.26.0 reaches MCP through mcpadapt 0.1.20, which imports streamablehttp_client from mcp.client.streamable_http, a name mcp 2.x no longer has, so it cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.
notes_by_num.15: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `map_mcp_content_to_tool_result_content` has no audio branch, so an audio block is dropped with a debug log, alone or beside other blocks.
notes_by_num.16: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0 requires @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.29.0, and on 1.30.0 it negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server: GenkitMcpClient opens every session with the legacy initialize handshake.
notes_by_num.17: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): depends on the boundary. `agent`: the `tool` message the provider receives is an empty string, and unlike an image the audio is not forwarded in a follow-up message. `direct`: `session.rpc.tools.execute` returns the `audio` block whole.
notes_by_num.18: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1 requires @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.26.0, and on 1.30.0 it negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server: MCPSessionManager opens every session with the legacy initialize handshake.
notes_by_num.19: Mastra 2.2.0: a result without `structuredContent` comes back unchanged, audio block intact. For a result that carries `structuredContent`, every content block is dropped, audio included; only the structured value reaches the agent.
notes_by_num.20: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the model receives an audio block as its JSON serialization inside a text item (`{"type":"audio",...}`); `MCPServer.callTool` itself returns the block intact.
notes_by_num.21: pi-mcp 0.99.1 negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server, because McpClient.connect opens every session with the legacy initialize handshake and its newest supported version is 2025-11-25.
notes_by_num.22: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): execute resolves with the CallToolResult, so a caller reading a step's toolResults gets the audio block intact. The adapter's toModelOutput converter maps only text and image blocks, so the model receives an audio block as a text part holding the block's JSON (type, MIME type and base64 data as characters). Boundary-dependent: kept at execute, flattened to text at model_output.
notes_by_num.23: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: The default `McpToolExecutor` result converter accepts text blocks only. Any `audio` block makes it throw `Unsupported content type: "audio"`: the direct executor raises it as a `RuntimeException`, and AiServices turns it into an error tool result the model reads in place of the block. notes_by_num.25: Koog 1.3.0-beta on the Kotlin MCP SDK 0.11.1 negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server: the SDK Client that McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient wraps offers only handshake-era protocol versions and never calls server/discover.
notes_by_num.26: spring-ai-starter-mcp-client 2.0.1 on MCP Java SDK 2.0.0 negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server: the SDK's McpClient offers only handshake-era protocol versions and never calls server/discover.
notes_by_num.27: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): a lone audio block becomes a `DataContent` with its bytes and MIME type at both boundaries. Beside `structuredContent` (`mixed_content`) `McpClientTool` returns the `CallToolResult` as JSON, so the audio reaches the model as base64 characters inside a text result, not as audio.
notes_by_num.28: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcpTool.Run` returns `{"output": text}`, where `formatMCPContent` replaces the block with a placeholder line (`[MCP audio: mimeType="audio/wav", size=44 bytes]`, with no audio data), and the model receives that map as `FunctionResponse.response`. When the result also has `structuredContent`, as in the mixed result, `Run` returns `{"output": structuredContent}` and the block is dropped.

tool-execution-errors.title: `isError`
tool-execution-errors.description: The in-band flag marking a tool result as a tool execution error, which the spec expects clients to pass to the model so it can correct itself.
tool-execution-errors.question: Can the agent tell a tool execution error from a successful result?
tool-execution-errors.notes: 2 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 9 changed or retained elsewhere, 2 dropped, 18 cannot reach MCP 2026-07-28. Measured at the value a direct invocation returns and at the value the framework's own agent path returns. Where those disagree, the cell is marked as boundary-dependent rather than dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` lists and calls tools only; it has no resource or prompt API, so a resources list_changed notification has nothing to refresh, and no hook hears it.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85 requires mcp>=1.30,<2.0, and on mcp 1.30.0 MCPTool.from_client negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server: MCPSessionProvider opens every session with the legacy initialize handshake.

notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26 requires MCP Python SDK 1.28.x (crewai pins mcp>=1.28.1,<1.29), so its native crewai.mcp client cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.

notes_by_num.13: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: at 2026-07-28 a change arrives only on a `subscriptions/listen` stream, and `MCPServerStdio` never opens one, so its `message_handler` heard nothing. At 2026-07-28 that notification travels only on a `subscriptions/listen` stream, which the toolset never opens, so the cache was never cleared and the next list was stale for the rest of the session.
notes_by_num.15: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0 requires mcp<2.0, and on mcp 1.26.0 its plugin negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server: MCPPluginBase opens every session with the legacy initialize handshake.
notes_by_num.16: smolagents 1.26.0 reaches MCP through mcpadapt 0.1.20, which imports streamablehttp_client from mcp.client.streamable_http, a name mcp 2.x no longer has, so it cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.
notes_by_num.17: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `on_tools_changed` is the only change hook, and it covers tools only. Nothing hears the resources notification, but `list_resources_sync` asks the server every time, so the next listing shows the change.

notes_by_num.20: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0 at 2026-07-28: the change is published on `subscriptions/listen`, which the SDK never opens; it shows only because the next `listResources` asks the server again.
notes_by_num.21: pi-mcp 0.99.1 negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server, because McpClient.connect opens every session with the legacy initialize handshake and its newest supported version is 2025-11-25.
notes_by_num.22: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): MCPClient opens no `subscriptions/listen` stream and registers no notification handler, so the change is never heard. `listResources()` fetches on every call, so the next list shows the added resource.
notes_by_num.23: ADK for Java 1.11.0 on MCP Java SDK 2.0.0 negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server: McpSessionManager builds an McpClient whose SDK offers only handshake-era protocol versions and never calls server/discover.

resource-subscriptions.question: Can the agent watch a single resource for changes?

notes_by_num.17: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPClient` opens `subscriptions/listen` itself, for tools list changes only and only when `on_tools_changed` is set. It hands the stream to no caller and has no subscribe API, so resource updates and other event kinds cannot be requested.
notes_by_num.18: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0 requires @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.29.0, and on 1.30.0 it negotiates 2025-11-25 against a 2026-07-28 server: GenkitMcpClient opens every session with the legacy initialize handshake.

known_issues: Measured by `scripts/measure_transports.py`: every renderer is asked for the fixture's tool definitions, resources, prompts and every result call over stdio, Streamable HTTP, with the fixture behind the recording proxy so the wire is logged on each. A transport is `y` when both fixtures open a session over it and, for an HTTP transport, every answer matches the stdio one.
At 2026-07-28 the row also reads the recorder's log of each POST: a request without `Mcp-Method`, or a `tools/call`, `prompts/get` or `resources/read` without `Mcp-Name`, marks the cell down.
transport-streamable-http.why: Every remote MCP server uses this transport, and 2026-07-28 changed it substantially: sessions and the `Mcp-Session-Id` header are gone, SSE resumability is gone, and two new headers are required. An adapter written for the old shape may connect and still be non-conformant.
